origins.section: Every LP Can Be Rewritten Into One Standard Form
Slack Is the Room Left in a ≤ Row, and Surplus Is the Excess Over a ≥ Row
A Row With Room Does Not Shape the Answer; Loosening It Changes Nothing

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-convert: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-convert: | $`a \cdot x \ge b`$ | $`-a \cdot x \le -b`$ | multiplying by $`-1`$ flips the inequality | ... | $`\min\, c^\top x`$ | $`\max\, (-c)^\top x`$, then negate the value | the lowest cost is minus the highest negative cost |
recorded.prompt:q-name-room: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-name-room: For a $`\le`$ row $`a \cdot x \le b`$, the **slack** is $`b - a \cdot x`$ ... For a $`\ge`$ row $`a \cdot x \ge b`$, the **surplus** is $`a \cdot x - b`$ ... Both are $`\ge 0`$ for any allowed solution, and both are $`0`$ exactly when the row is full. A row whose slack or surplus is zero at the solution is called **binding**
recorded.prompt:q-drop-row: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.outcome:q-drop-row: The floor had $12.0k of surplus; deleting the floor altogether changes nothing. A row with room was not pressing on the solution, so moving it, or removing it, leaves the best split allowed and still best.
